comments.author: @SarahSalter-s8p
comments.text: I live in Orting WA. Our city is right under Mt Rainier. The two rivers in this valley (Carbon River & Puyallup River) put us in the exact path of the most dangerous risk. Thr lahar path. We have ONE highway out of this valley. One lane each direction. Pierce County WA has done nothing about this. One car accident on a road shuts down a road. Trapping the cities residents & employees at work. Lahar sirens don't help if you can't leave the area due to panic which has a 100% of stopping ALL traffic. All official literature says the chance of major lahar event is one in six in my lifetime. This is word for word what's posted by our county & cities. Found in our DMV's. City halls. Police depts. All public libraries & more. Our local govt here in Pierce County WA is negligent. One in six. One highway with one lane. Panic while driving will overcome MOST drivers. That's the science. We're all dead here. My family is moving due to this. We are one of only a handful of residents moving. Again...even our local businesses (UPS, Fed Ex,  grocery stores, etc) all have the one in six charts posted for residents. These posters are the only official literature we received. This is the exact same poster & info on the literature mailed to all area residents notifying them why lahar sirens were being installed. The literature has never changed a single word in the 16 yrs it's been posted.

comments.author: @deadlyknights1119
comments.text: I've lived on Nevada-Cali border for most of my life. Often I would travel up to my cousins in Spokane and it was such an emotional drive to leave the desert valley and enter the mountain forests of Oregon where you can almost always see one of these Cascade behemoths in the distance. Adams, Hood, Crater Lake, Whitney, and Reiner are all so striking for their prominence compared to the valleys around them, especially Mt Hood and Reiner. Sometimes we'd go through Northern California and get to see Mt Shasta. It was an otherworldly experience driving by mountains so tall they had glaciers in NORTHERN CALIFORNIA. The cascades and the forests that surround them are such a great vacation spot for the Late spring through Autumn.
